summary: Sustained mini-burst shadowing causing gradual GPU credit leakage and p99 throughput spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer LexiDocs on a dedicated pool is observing gradual throughput degradation at p99 over ~6 hour windows coincident with many short-lived inference streams. Impact: intermittent request spikes, elevated p99 latency (3-10x), occasional 429s and autoscaler failing to add capacity fast enough. Environment: production dedicated cluster in us-west-2 serving the redwood/gpt-4o-instruct-2.7b-quant4x variant. Observed since 2026-03-09 23:30 UTC and recurring daily during customer batch windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs high rate of short-lived streams (avg duration < 2s) with modest concurrency per connection.
2) Multiple cohorts (50-300 small streams) align causing prefetcher to issue many KV cache fills and small batch allocations.
3) Serving runtime reports increased attach latency and autoscaler telemetry shows rapid decrement in 'available_gpu_credit' for the dedicated pool.
4) Result: p99 latency spikes, some requests receive 429s while autoscaler attempts to reconcile capacity.
Note: Issue is intermittent and correlates to customer traffic patterns rather than a single stack change.
observed_behavior: During alignment windows: p50 remains near baseline (~45ms) while p99 increases from 200ms up to 1.2s; autoscaler reports 'credit_quota_drain' and does not provision new nodes for 30-90s. Telemetry shows KV cache growth spikes and scheduler queue length increases. GPU attach timeouts and a handful of 5xxs observed in the window.
expected_behavior: Autoscaler should provision/reserve additional capacity within configured cooldown such that p99 stays within SLO (<350ms) and 429/5xx rates remain negligible for dedicated customers on committed capacity.
comments: 2026-03-10 01:15 - Riley Nguyen (SRE): Acknowledged. Initial triage shows synchronized short-stream fanout from LexiDocs region causing prefetcher to queue; autoscaler saw rapid GPU credit usage and stayed in cooldown. Collecting allocator and prefetcher traces.

2026-03-10 02:05 - Marcus Patel (Customer Success): Customer confirms they have a new analytics job that spawns thousands of ephemeral streams during the midnight window; they can throttle but would prefer platform-side mitigation.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Riley Nguyen (SRE): Applied temporary reserved burst (added 2x small GPU units) to LexiDocs dedicated pool to absorb immediate load spike. Observed p99 drop back toward baseline within 2 minutes.
2026-03-12 14:40 - Engineering (serving-runtime): We have a follow-up PR to alter prefetch coordination and expose a per-tenant prefetch cap. Planning rollout to staging this week.

2026-03-12 16:00 - Customer (LexiDocs Ops): Appreciative of temporary reserve; asks for guidance on client-side pacing and whether Redwood can implement graceful retry rate-limiting for short streams.
investigation_notes: - Aggregated allocator metrics show 'available_gpu_credit' decreasing in a sawtooth pattern synchronized with customer mini-burst windows.
- Prefetcher traces reveal many concurrent KV fill requests hitting the same shard; this causes IO bursts and GPU attach backpressure.
- Autoscaler decision logs show multiple missed scale-ups because 'credit_usage_rate' crossed threshold then fell before cooldown expired, causing oscillation and underprovisioning.
- No single driver or node-level failure observed; the pattern is an emergent effect of many short streams causing small batch fragmentation and KV cache churn.
- Related historical tickets indicate similar symptoms but different root triggers (SUP-271400, SUP-742001).
hypotheses: 1) Prefetch cohort resonance: many small streams align causing synchronous KV prefetches and temporary IO saturation which indirectly increases GPU attach latency.
2) Autoscaler sensitivity too coarse for high-frequency microbursts; cooldown prevents timely capacity expansion leading to p99 spikes.
3) Tenant-level GPU credit accounting undercounts transient reservations from prefetcher, creating a perceived leak that prevents fast allocation.
4) Client traffic pattern (short-lived connections) causes slot fragmentation and reduces batch efficiency, amplifying resource pressure.
mitigation: Short-term (applied 2026-03-11 09:30): Added temporary reserved burst to LexiDocs dedicated pool and increased autoscaler max-rate for the pool to allow quicker short-term provisioning.
Immediate customer guidance: Requested LexiDocs throttle spawn rate of ephemeral streams during 00:00-06:00 UTC and phase their job to reduce cohort alignment.
Workaround: Enable per-tenant small-stream rate-limiter and reduce prefetch concurrency for the dedicated pool (config change staged).
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: temporary reserved capacity and autoscaler adjustments reduced p99 spikes during windows. Root cause under investigation; engineering to deploy targeted prefetch caps and autoscaler tuning to prevent recurrence.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering to land PR that adds per-tenant prefetch caps and a more responsive autoscaler policy (related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prefetcher/pull/118).
2) Ops to run a controlled canary in us-west-2 for the new prefetch cap and autoscaler parameters (scheduled 2026-03-15).
3) Customer Success to provide LexiDocs with client pacing recommendations and a short-term config snippet for exponential backoff on ephemeral streams.
4) Postmortem checklist entry to monitor for similar 'mini-burst cohort' patterns and add an alert rule for synchronized KV prefetch spikes.
5) Billing/contract review to discuss whether customer needs a higher reserved burst tier for predictable high-frequency short-stream workloads.
